No `version` statement in any do-file. Stata's behaviour depends on the version, so a rerun must choose one and log it.
Julia code without a Manifest.toml: package versions are not pinned.
10 code lines use absolute paths from the authors' machines. A rerun must edit them, and each edit is a logged deviation.
The README is not plain text (README.pdf). Triage cannot read it, so the data availability statement, licence and run time below were not checked against it. Read it by hand.
Requires Stata; the desk says it has it.

Files the code both writes and reads are already in the package: $MyPath/Save/prices.dta, $MyPath/Save/prices_synthetic.dta, $MyPath/Save/sector_scons.dta, $MyPath/data/worldscope/worldscope.csv, $MyPath/save/bycohort_cov.dta, $MyPath/save/bycohort_secondorder_transactions.dta, $MyPath/save/bycohort_synthetic.dta, $MyPath/save/bycohort_welfare_baseline.dta, $MyPath/save/bycohort_welfare_collateral.dta, $MyPath/save/bycohort_welfare_combine.dta. A run may read these instead of recomputing them. A receipt must say whether it replayed them or recomputed them, and a matching output hash alone does not show recomputation.
58 file reads use paths built at run time (macros, globs, variables), so triage could not check that those inputs exist.
No licence file and no licence named in the documentation. Running it for a check is unaffected, but a receipt should quote and hash files rather than redistribute them.
